question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.title: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
events.description:

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s entrenched position within the Chinese Communist Party drives the near-certain trader consensus that he will remain in power through 2027. Following the abolition of presidential term limits and his third term at the 20th Party Congress, Xi has continued consolidating authority through military and civilian leadership purges, leaving few independent power centers or designated successors in the Politburo Standing Committee. The 21st Party Congress, scheduled for late 2027, is widely viewed as the venue for confirming a fourth term rather than a transition. Occasional rumors of health issues, delegation of authority, or elite infighting have surfaced but lack substantiation in official channels or verifiable events. While a sudden medical development, major external crisis, or unanticipated internal challenge could still shift the timeline, the absence of structural mechanisms or organized opposition makes such outcomes improbable before the resolution window.
